title: Tech Note: Creating a Program Item with a Custom Icon to Launch Your Executable File on Windows
author: Julie Pearson
featured_technology: Windows 95 Start Menu / Windows NT & 3.1x Program Manager

historical_commentary.text: This note walks through OS-level Windows 95/NT/3.1 shell mechanics (Program Manager groups, Start Menu shortcuts, .ico files) for giving a compiled/merged 4D Engine application a custom icon, since the merge process produced separate EXE/4DC/RSR files with a generic icon rather than a single polished executable. The underlying need — a distinct icon for a distributed executable — is still relevant today, but the specific instructions are entirely tied to Windows 3.1/95/NT-era shell UI (Program Manager, Taskbar Properties dialogs) that no longer exists in any current Windows version, and the 4D Compiler Pro / merge-with-4D-Engine deployment model itself has been superseded.
related_updates: Windows 3.1/NT Program Manager and the described Windows 95 Taskbar Properties dialogs no longer exist in any supported version of Windows

4D's compiled/merged application build process has evolved substantially; modern 4D build tools (Build Application) generate a single application executable with icon customization handled directly in the build settings, rather than requiring manual OS-level shortcut/icon assignment after merging with 4D Engine
